changes.before: Three methods; proposed split awaiting consistency adjudication. Complete printed support notes and allocation: 1. Questionnaire: Can be given to the organisation visited as well as to the class. Reason: Easy to administer/collate results. Can be completed anonymously. Generally inexpensive. Good response rate. They are objective. 2. Ask Teachers/Member of organisation visited for their opinion. Reason: Allows the class to practice their interview/communication skills. Questions can be explained if necessary. Easy to do. No cost involved. You will get honest feedback/review of teamwork. 3. Quality of report - has enough information/correct type of information been learned? Reason: Easy method to use as all class members must produce a report. Reports can be compared easily. 4. Review of Teamwork – to see if the class put into practice what they have learned. Reason Objective was to work well as a team. All class members are aware of what is involved. 5. Class Discussion: Varying opinions and discussions can be taken on board. Reason Easy to organise Everyone can participate. Allows one to see how much was learned. Good to show improvement or practice in communication skills. 3 @ 2m (1 + 1)

changes.before: Proposed positive-effect card, with all seven positive models. The six negative models are shown for source context only. Third-reader validation required. Complete original wording, models and allocation: Describe one positive and one negative effect for an enterprising moving to selling online. Two valid answers 2 x 2 marks (1+1) 1. You can shop at any time. 2. You do not need a shop for online so rent will be cheaper. 3. More stock on hand as area for shop sales is not reduced/warehouse. 4. Online platform can develop a bigger audience/customer base than a shop base. 5. Selling Online can offer promo discount codes. 6. Online sales can have reviews. 7. Hours of work different which may be easier to attract staff with selling online. 1. Dealing with returns is more complex/time 2. You have to consider costs such as packaging or delivery dates with online. 3. With online you need a good website/product description to make it easy for customers to order. 4. Greater security risks/fees to be paid for online payments. 5. Better relationship/rapport/attention with in person sales. People can be distracted when on line with ads, social media, and other websites competing for attention. 6. Losing customers who do not have access/use the internet.

Marketing/Market Research ‐ to find out if your idea will be successful: Desk and field research/undertaken by the business or by a market research firm/identify target market/demand/competition/advertising/USP/price. 2. Finance ‐ to know how much is needed/where you will get the money/budgeting is important to ensure you have enough to meet your running costs. Sources of finance/loan/grants/cash flow forecast/budgeting income and expenditure/costs involved in purchasing equipment. 3. Staff/Personnel/HR ‐ to know how many employees are required/qualifications: Job description for employees/qualifications/salary/training required/how many employees needed. 4. Production ‐ to know how long it will take to make the product/potential difficulties can be planned for. Raw materials/suppliers/production process/distribution/packaging/design. 5. Location/Premises ‐ to plan for proper facilities and enough space/near good infrastructure. Near customers, staff and suppliers/parking/adequate room for future expansion. Near airport/good road network for deliveries. 6. Legalities – planning permission, custom clearance, safety statement, employee contracts.
